name: Tricky Words
description: 34 German particles whose meaning depends on context: damit, doch, eben, halt, ja, mal, ruhig, schon, etc.

items.prompt: Ich schreibe damit einen Brief. (damit means…)
items.explanation: Here *damit* is a pronominal adverb meaning *with it* — referring back to the writing instrument. Compare *damit* as a conjunction meaning *so that*.

items.prompt: Ich lerne Deutsch, damit ich in Zürich arbeiten kann. (damit means…)
items.explanation: *damit* introducing a purpose clause = *so that*. Different from pronominal *damit* = *with it/that*.

items.prompt: Was willst du damit sagen? (damit means…)
items.explanation: Pronominal *damit* = *by that* — referring back to the prior statement. Different from conjunction *damit* = *so that*.

items.prompt: Er spart Geld, damit er reisen kann. (damit means…)
items.explanation: *damit* as a purpose conjunction = *so that*, sending the verb to the end. Different from pronominal *damit* = *with it*.

items.prompt: Wie viel hast du dafür bezahlt? (dafür means…)
items.explanation: Pronominal *dafür* = *for it* — the price paid for the thing referenced. Different from contrastive *dafür* = *on the other hand*.

items.prompt: Er ist streng, dafür ist er fair. (dafür means…)
items.explanation: Contrastive *dafür* = *on the other hand / to make up for it* — balancing a negative with a positive. Different from literal *dafür* = *for it*.

items.prompt: Ich bin dafür. (dafür means…)
items.explanation: *dafür sein* = *to be in favor of it* — the standard pro/contra idiom. Different from compensatory *dafür* = *on the other hand*.

items.prompt: Dafür kann ich nichts. (dafür means…)
items.explanation: Idiomatic *dafür kann ich nichts* = *I can't help it / it's not my fault about that*. Different from literal *dafür* = *for it (in exchange)*.

items.prompt: Was sagst du dazu? (dazu means…)
items.explanation: Pronominal *dazu* = *about that* — referring back to a topic just raised. Different from additive *dazu* = *in addition*.

items.prompt: Er kocht gut, und dazu singt er auch. (dazu means…)
items.explanation: Additive *dazu* = *in addition / on top of that*, stacking another quality. Different from *dazu* = *about that* (reference) or *for that purpose*.

items.prompt: Dazu brauche ich mehr Zeit. (dazu means…)
items.explanation: *dazu* = *for that purpose / to do that* — referring to a task to accomplish. Different from additive *dazu* = *in addition*.

items.prompt: Ich habe keine Lust dazu. (dazu means…)
items.explanation: *Lust dazu* — *dazu* refers back to the activity: *no desire to do that*. Different from additive *dazu* = *in addition*.

items.prompt: Bist du schon fertig? (schon means…)
items.explanation: *schon* meaning *already* (sooner than expected). Different from modal-particle *schon* reassuring the listener.

items.prompt: Das wird schon klappen. (schon means…)
items.explanation: Modal-particle *schon* in a future statement = *surely / don't worry, it'll work out*. Different from temporal *schon* = *already*.

items.prompt: Ich habe schon drei Mal angerufen. (schon means…)
items.explanation: *schon* = *already*, marking that an action has occurred more times than expected. Different from reassuring *schon* = *don't worry*.

items.prompt: Das ist schon okay. (schon means…)
items.explanation: Modal-particle *schon* softens the statement = *it's alright / fine really*. Different from temporal *schon* = *already*.

items.prompt: Er schläft noch. (noch means…)
items.explanation: *noch* meaning *still* (the action continues). Compare *noch ein* = *another*, *noch nicht* = *not yet*.

items.prompt: Noch ein Bier, bitte! (noch means…)
items.explanation: *noch ein* = *another / one more*. Different from *noch* = *still* (continuing action) or *noch* = *even* (intensifier).

items.prompt: Das ist noch besser als das erste. (noch means…)
items.explanation: *noch* before a comparative = *even (better)*, intensifying the comparison. Different from *noch* = *still* (continuing).

items.prompt: Hast du noch Fragen? (noch means…)
items.explanation: *noch* in a question = *any more / further* — checking for remaining items. Different from *noch* = *still* (continuing action).

items.prompt: Er kommt erst morgen. (erst means…)
items.explanation: Temporal *erst* = *not until* — later than expected. Opposite of *schon* = *already*. Different from sequential *erst* = *first*.

items.prompt: Ich bin erst angekommen. (erst means…)
items.explanation: *erst* = *only just / just now* — emphasising how recent the action is. Different from sequential *erst* = *first*.

items.prompt: Erst denken, dann handeln. (erst means…)
items.explanation: Sequential *erst … dann …* = *first … then …*. Different from temporal *erst* = *not until* or quantitative *erst* = *only*.

items.prompt: Sie ist erst fünf Jahre alt. (erst means…)
items.explanation: Quantitative *erst* with an age or quantity = *only / just* (less than you'd think). Different from *erst* = *first* (sequential).

items.prompt: — Du kommst nicht mit? — Doch! (doch means…)
items.explanation: Standalone *doch!* contradicts a negative statement = *yes, I am!*. Different from modal-particle *doch* softening an imperative.

items.prompt: Das weißt du doch! (doch means…)
items.explanation: Modal-particle *doch* insisting on shared knowledge = *come on, you know that!*. Different from *doch* contradicting a negation.

items.prompt: Komm doch mit! (doch means…)
items.explanation: Modal-particle *doch* softening an imperative — *go ahead and come along*. Different from *doch* contradicting a negation.

items.prompt: Er kommt doch. (doch means…)
items.explanation: *doch* meaning *after all / yet* — contradicting a prior expectation that he wouldn't come. Different from softening *doch* in imperatives.

items.prompt: Das ist ja klar! (ja means…)
items.explanation: Modal-particle *ja* marks shared/obvious knowledge = *obviously / as we both know*. Different from *ja* as a warning or as a literal *yes*.

items.prompt: Komm ja nicht zu spät! (ja means…)
items.explanation: Modal-particle *ja* in a negative imperative is a strong warning = *don't you dare*. Different from *ja* marking shared knowledge = *obviously*.

items.prompt: Hör mal! (mal means…)
items.explanation: Modal-particle *mal* softens an imperative = *just listen for a sec*. Different from temporal *mal* = *once / at some point*.

items.prompt: Ich war mal in Berlin. (mal means…)
items.explanation: Temporal *mal* with past tense = *once / at some point*, short for *einmal*. Different from softening *mal* in imperatives.

items.prompt: Wo bist du denn? (denn means…)
items.explanation: Modal-particle *denn* in a question softens it and signals curiosity. Different from coordinating *denn* = *because*.

items.prompt: Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin müde. (denn means…)
items.explanation: Coordinating *denn* = *because* — note that the clause keeps verb-second order, unlike *weil*.

items.prompt: Er ist wohl krank. (wohl means…)
items.explanation: *wohl* meaning *probably* — a hedged guess about the situation. Different from *wohl* in a question expressing wonder or disbelief.

items.prompt: Was meint er wohl damit? (wohl means…)
items.explanation: *wohl* in a question marks musing = *I wonder*. Different from declarative *wohl* = *probably*.

items.prompt: Ich fahre nach Zürich. (nach means…)
items.explanation: *nach* + city/country = *to* (directional). Different from *nach* + dative time = *after*, or *nach + Meinung* = *according to*.

items.prompt: Nach dem Essen gehen wir spazieren. (nach means…)
items.explanation: *nach* + dative for time *after*. Different from *nach* + city = *to*, or *nach + Meinung* = *according to*.

items.prompt: Meiner Meinung nach ist das falsch. (nach means…)
items.explanation: Postposed *nach* in *Meinung nach* = *according to*. Different from *nach* + city = *to* or *nach* + time = *after*.

items.prompt: Wir fahren nach Hause. (nach means…)
items.explanation: Idiomatic *nach Hause* = *(to) home* — direction. Different from locative *zu Hause* = *at home*, or *nach* = *after*.

items.prompt: Ich bin krank, somit kann ich nicht zur Arbeit kommen. (somit means…)
items.explanation: *somit* drawing a logical conclusion = *therefore / thus*. Different from causal *weil* / *denn* = *because*, which give a reason rather than a result.

items.prompt: Alle Tests sind bestanden. Somit ist das Projekt abgeschlossen. (somit means…)
items.explanation: *somit* linking a closing consequence = *with that / and so*. Different from purely logical *somit* = *therefore*, this one wraps up a sequence.

items.prompt: Keine Sorge, ich komme sowieso vorbei. (sowieso means…)
items.explanation: *sowieso* = *anyway / in any case* — the action is happening regardless. Different from *sowieso* implying obvious shared knowledge.

items.prompt: Das weiß ich sowieso schon. (sowieso means…)
items.explanation: *sowieso* here = *of course / obviously already*, dismissing the info as redundant. Different from plan-related *sowieso* = *I was going to anyway*.

items.prompt: Es regnet, trotzdem gehe ich spazieren. (trotzdem means…)
items.explanation: *trotzdem* = *nevertheless* — going ahead despite an obstacle. Different from causal *deshalb* = *therefore*, which would mean rain made you go.

items.prompt: Das war nicht nötig, aber trotzdem danke! (trotzdem means…)
items.explanation: *trotzdem* softened to *all the same / still* — gratitude despite the gift being unnecessary. Different from the stronger contrastive *trotzdem* = *nevertheless*.

items.prompt: Das Essen war gut, allerdings war es teuer. (allerdings means…)
items.explanation: *allerdings* introducing a qualification = *however / but*. Different from emphatic *allerdings!* = *absolutely!* as a standalone reply.

items.prompt: Allerdings muss ich zugeben, dass er recht hat. (allerdings means…)
items.explanation: Sentence-initial *allerdings* conceding a point = *admittedly*. Different from mid-sentence *allerdings* = *however*, or exclamatory *allerdings!* = *absolutely!*.

items.prompt: — Kommst du zur Party? — Allerdings! (allerdings means…)
items.explanation: Standalone *Allerdings!* as a reply = *absolutely!* — emphatic agreement. Different from connective *allerdings* = *however / admittedly*.

items.prompt: Er ist zwar klug, aber faul. (zwar means…)
items.explanation: *zwar* meaning *admittedly* — paired with a later *aber* in the classic *zwar … aber …* construction. Different from *und zwar* = *specifically*.

items.prompt: Ich habe zwar wenig Zeit, aber ich helfe dir trotzdem. (zwar means…)
items.explanation: *zwar* conceding before an *aber* = *granted / true*. Different from *und zwar* = *namely / specifically*.

items.prompt: Ich komme, und zwar morgen früh. (zwar means…)
items.explanation: *und zwar* introducing a specification = *specifically / to be exact*. Different from concessive *zwar … aber …* = *admittedly … but …*.

items.prompt: Ich habe nur ein Problem, nämlich die Miete. (nämlich means…)
items.explanation: *nämlich* spelling out a specific case = *namely*. Different from causal mid-sentence *nämlich* = *because / you see*.

items.prompt: Er kommt heute nicht. Er ist nämlich krank. (nämlich means…)
items.explanation: Mid-sentence *nämlich* gives an explanation = *because / you see*. Different from *nämlich* introducing a specific item = *namely*.

items.prompt: So ist es eben. (eben means…)
options: simply / just the way it is
items.answer: simply / just the way it is
items.explanation: Modal-particle *eben* expressing resignation = *simply / that's just how it is*. Compare temporal *eben* = *just now* or agreement *eben!* = *exactly!*.

items.prompt: Er ist eben angekommen. (eben means…)
items.explanation: *eben* meaning *just now* (temporal). Compare *eben* meaning *exactly* (agreement) or *simply* (resignation).

items.prompt: — Das ist unfair! — Eben! (eben means…)
items.explanation: Standalone *Eben!* = *exactly!* — emphatic agreement. Different from temporal *eben* = *just now* or resigned *eben* = *simply*.

items.prompt: Das ist halt so in der Schweiz. (halt means…)
options: simply / just the way it is
items.answer: simply / just the way it is
items.explanation: Modal-particle *halt* (Southern German / Swiss equivalent of *eben*) expressing resignation = *that's just how it is*. Different from the imperative *Halt!* = *stop!*.

items.prompt: Halt! Nicht weitergehen! (halt means…)
items.explanation: Imperative *Halt!* = *stop!* — from the verb *halten*. Different from modal-particle *halt* = *simply / just the way it is*.

items.prompt: Was machst du eigentlich beruflich? (eigentlich means…)
items.explanation: Modal-particle *eigentlich* in a question = *actually / by the way*, broaching a new topic. Different from *eigentlich* = *originally* or *strictly speaking*.

items.prompt: Eigentlich wollte ich kommen, aber ich bin krank. (eigentlich means…)
items.explanation: *eigentlich* + *wollte* = *originally / I had meant to* — a plan that didn't happen. Different from conversational *eigentlich* = *by the way*.

items.prompt: Das ist eigentlich nicht erlaubt. (eigentlich means…)
items.explanation: *eigentlich* qualifying a rule = *strictly speaking* (with an implied *but*). Different from *eigentlich* = *originally* or conversational *eigentlich* = *by the way*.

items.prompt: Beeil dich, sonst verpassen wir den Zug. (sonst means…)
items.explanation: *sonst* meaning *otherwise* (consequence of not acting). Compare *sonst* = *else / any other* in questions, or *sonst* = *usually*.

items.prompt: Haben Sie sonst noch Fragen? (sonst means…)
items.explanation: *sonst noch* in a question = *any other / else*. Different from *sonst* = *otherwise* (consequence) or *sonst* = *usually*.

items.prompt: Sonst trinke ich keinen Kaffee, aber heute brauche ich einen. (sonst means…)
items.explanation: *sonst* contrasted with *heute* = *usually / normally*. Different from *sonst* = *otherwise* (warning) or *sonst* = *else*.

items.prompt: Ich verstehe das überhaupt nicht. (überhaupt means…)
items.explanation: *überhaupt* meaning *at all* — emphasising a negation. Different from *überhaupt* meaning *in general* or *in the first place*.

items.prompt: Warst du überhaupt dort? (überhaupt means…)
items.explanation: *überhaupt* in a question challenging a premise = *even / in the first place*. Different from negation-intensifying *überhaupt* = *at all*.

items.prompt: Überhaupt finde ich das eine gute Idee. (überhaupt means…)
items.explanation: Sentence-initial *überhaupt* = *in general / on the whole*. Different from negation-intensifying *überhaupt* = *at all*.

items.prompt: Keine Sorge, ich gehe ohnehin einkaufen. (ohnehin means…)
items.explanation: *ohnehin* = *anyway / in any case* — the action is happening regardless. Near-synonym of *sowieso*. Different from *ohnehin* = *already / as it is*.

items.prompt: Er ist ohnehin spät dran. (ohnehin means…)
items.explanation: *ohnehin* describing an existing situation = *already / as it is*. Different from plan-related *ohnehin* = *anyway*, this stresses the current state.

items.prompt: Ich komme jedenfalls. (jedenfalls means…)
options: in any case / at any rate
items.answer: in any case / at any rate
items.explanation: *jedenfalls* = *in any case / at any rate* — committing to an action regardless. Different from narrowing *jedenfalls* = *at least* (limiting a claim).

items.prompt: Er hat es jedenfalls versucht. (jedenfalls means…)
items.explanation: *jedenfalls* narrowing the scope of a claim = *at least he tried (whatever else is true)*. Different from commitment-style *jedenfalls* = *in any case*.

items.prompt: Es regnet, aber immerhin ist es warm. (immerhin means…)
items.explanation: *immerhin* as a silver lining = *at least* (consolation). Different from *immerhin* = *after all / considering*, which justifies leniency.

items.prompt: Immerhin ist er noch ein Kind. (immerhin means…)
items.explanation: *immerhin* introducing a mitigating fact = *after all / considering*. Different from *immerhin* offering a silver lining = *at least*.

items.prompt: Vielleicht kommt er morgen. (vielleicht means…)
items.explanation: *vielleicht* meaning *maybe*. Modal-particle *vielleicht* can also express exasperation in exclamations or soften a suggestion.

items.prompt: Gehen wir vielleicht ins Kino? (vielleicht means…)
items.explanation: Modal-particle *vielleicht* softening a proposal = *maybe we should …*. Different from epistemic *vielleicht* = *maybe / perhaps*.

items.prompt: Das ist vielleicht eine Frechheit! (vielleicht means…)
items.explanation: Exclamatory *vielleicht* = *what a / really* — intensifying outrage, not hedging. Different from literal *vielleicht* = *maybe*.

items.prompt: Er ist gerade angekommen. (gerade means…)
items.explanation: *gerade* meaning *just now / right now* — actions in progress at the moment of speech. Different from emphatic *gerade* = *exactly* or adjectival *gerade* = *straight*.

items.prompt: Gerade das wollte ich sagen. (gerade means…)
items.explanation: Emphatic *gerade* highlighting a specific thing = *exactly / precisely that*. Different from temporal *gerade* = *just now*.

items.prompt: Der Weg ist gerade. (gerade means…)
items.explanation: *gerade* as an adjective/adverb = *straight*. Different from temporal *gerade* = *just now*.

items.prompt: Warum gerade ich? (gerade means…)
items.explanation: *gerade* emphasising an unwelcome choice = *of all people*. Different from temporal *gerade* = *just now* or geometric *gerade* = *straight*.

items.prompt: Ich komme gleich. (gleich means…)
items.explanation: Temporal *gleich* = *right away / in a moment*. Different from comparative *gleich* = *the same* or idiomatic *mir gleich* = *doesn't matter*.

items.prompt: Wir sind gleich alt. (gleich means…)
items.explanation: *gleich* as a comparative adjective = *the same*. Different from temporal *gleich* = *in a moment*.

items.prompt: Das ist mir gleich. (gleich means…)
items.explanation: Idiomatic *mir gleich* = *all the same to me / doesn't matter*. Different from temporal *gleich* = *right away* or comparative *gleich* = *the same*.

items.prompt: Er kann sogar Chinesisch. (sogar means…)
items.explanation: *sogar* adding a surprising extra = *even*. Compare *noch* = *even* (intensifying a comparative); *sogar* spotlights an unexpected item.

items.prompt: Heute ist es sogar besser als gestern. (sogar means…)
items.explanation: *sogar* before a comparative = *even (better)*, marking surprise at the degree. Compare *noch besser* = *still better*, a more neutral intensifier.

items.prompt: Du denkst zu viel — mach es einfach! (einfach means…)
items.explanation: Modal-particle *einfach* = *just (do it)* — urging direct action. Different from adjectival *einfach* = *easy* or ticket *einfach* = *one-way*.

items.prompt: Dieses Problem ist ziemlich einfach. (einfach means…)
items.explanation: Adjectival *einfach* = *easy / simple*. Different from modal-particle *einfach* = *just (do it)* or ticket *einfach* = *one-way*.

items.prompt: Eine einfache Fahrt nach Bern, bitte. (einfach means…)
items.explanation: *einfache Fahrt* = *one-way trip* (vs. *Hin- und Rückfahrt*). Different from adjectival *einfach* = *easy* or modal-particle *einfach* = *just*.

items.prompt: Es war lediglich ein Missverständnis. (lediglich means…)
items.explanation: *lediglich* = *merely / just*, downplaying the seriousness — a formal cousin of *nur*. Different from softening *lediglich* used to make a request modest.

items.prompt: Ich möchte lediglich eine Frage stellen. (lediglich means…)
items.explanation: *lediglich* softening a request = *just / only* — formal politeness marker. Different from dismissive *lediglich* = *merely* (downplaying an event).

items.prompt: Wenigstens du bist da! (wenigstens means…)
items.explanation: *wenigstens* expressing relief = *at least* (small comfort). Different from *wenigstens* as a bare-minimum demand, and from quantitative *mindestens* = *at least N*.

items.prompt: Sag wenigstens Hallo! (wenigstens means…)
items.explanation: *wenigstens* demanding the bare minimum = *at least say hello*. Different from consoling *wenigstens* = *at least (relief)*, and from numerical *mindestens*.

items.prompt: Das kostet mindestens 100 Euro. (mindestens means…)
items.explanation: *mindestens* = *at least* with numbers — a lower bound. Different from emotional *wenigstens* = *at least (relief / minimum ask)*.

items.prompt: Wir brauchen mindestens drei Stunden. (mindestens means…)
items.explanation: *mindestens* with a duration = *at least N hours* — a quantitative floor. Different from emotive *wenigstens* = *at least (relief)*.
